content: 1. The indicator for new and relapse cases of pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) that are bacteriologically confirmed is calculated as the number of such cases registered for treatment multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of new and relapse pulmonary TB cases. This data is reported quarterly and annually, using district TB laboratory and treatment registers. 2. The sputum positivity rate is determined by dividing the number of new and relapse TB cases (bacteriologically confirmed) by the total number of new individuals with respiratory symptoms investigated, then multiplying by 100. This is reported quarterly and annually, based on TB laboratory registers. 3. The bacteriological confirmation rate is calculated as the number of new and relapse pulmonary TB cases (bacteriologically confirmed) multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of new and relapse pulmonary TB cases registered. This is reported quarterly and annually, using TB treatment registers. 4. The percentage of initial lost-to-follow-up cases is calculated as the number of new and relapse pulmonary TB cases registered for treatment multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of new pulmonary TB cases (bacteriologically confirmed). This is reported quarterly and annually, using TB laboratory and treatment registers. 5. The percentage of eligible TB contacts who started latent TB infection (LTBI) treatment is calculated as the number of individuals who started LTBI treatment because they were eligible. This is reported quarterly and annually, using TB contact registers. 6. The percentage of new and relapse TB cases not evaluated for treatment outcome is calculated as the number of such cases multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of new and relapse TB cases registered for treatment. This is reported quarterly and annually, using quarterly treatment outcome reports. 7. The treatment success rate is calculated as the number of new and relapse TB cases successfully treated multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of new and relapse TB cases registered for treatment. This is reported monthly, quarterly, and annually, using National Tuberculosis Programme (NTP) records. 8. The percentage of TB cases lost to follow-up is calculated as the number of new and relapse TB cases lost to follow-up multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of new and relapse TB cases registered for treatment. This is reported quarterly and annually, using NTP records. 9. The TB case fatality rate is calculated as the number of TB deaths divided by the total number of TB cases notified for treatment, then multiplied by 100. This is reported monthly, quarterly, and annually, using facility registers. Data is disaggregated by sex, age group (0–4, 5–14, 15+), HIV status, and TB drug resistance. 10. The percentage of people with TB receiving social support is calculated as the number of individuals with TB who received social support. This is reported quarterly and annually, using NTP records. 11. The multidrug-resistant/rifampicin-resistant TB (MDR/RR-TB) case detection rate is calculated as the number of new MDR/RR-TB cases notified multiplied by 100, divided by the estimated number of new MDR/RR-TB cases. This is reported annually, using NTP records. 12. The MDR-TB treatment success rate is calculated as the number of MDR-TB cases successfully treated multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of MDR-TB cases registered for treatment. This is reported quarterly and annually, using district TB treatment registers. 13. The percentage of people living with HIV screened for active TB is calculated as the number of individuals living with HIV who were screened for TB multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of people living with HIV. This is reported quarterly and annually, using HIV service records. 14. The percentage of people living with HIV newly enrolled in HIV care who started TB preventive therapy is calculated as the number of such individuals who started treatment for LTBI multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of people living with HIV newly enrolled in HIV care. This is reported quarterly and annually, using HIV records. 15. The percentage of registered new/relapse TB cases with documented HIV status is calculated as the number of new and relapse TB cases with a recorded HIV test result multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of new and relapse TB cases registered in the TB register. This is reported quarterly and annually, using NTP records. 16. The percentage of registered new/relapse TB cases documented as HIV-positive is calculated as the number of new and relapse TB cases documented as HIV-positive multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of new and relapse TB cases with documented HIV status. This is reported quarterly and annually, using NTP records. 17. The percentage of HIV-positive new/relapse TB cases placed on antiretroviral therapy (ART) during TB treatment is calculated as the number of such cases who started or were already on ART during TB treatment multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of HIV-positive new/relapse TB cases registered. This is reported quarterly and annually, using NTP records. 18. The case fatality rate among HIV-positive new/relapse TB cases is calculated as the number of HIV-positive new/relapse TB cases who died during TB treatment multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of HIV-positive new/relapse TB cases registered for treatment. This is reported quarterly and annually, using NTP records. 19. The percentage of HIV-positive new/relapse TB cases who received co-trimoxazole preventive therapy is calculated as the number of such cases who started or continued co-trimoxazole preventive therapy during TB treatment multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of HIV-positive new/relapse TB cases registered. This is reported quarterly and annually, using NTP records. 20. The percentage of new/relapse TB cases among children under 5 years is calculated as the number of such cases by age group and sex multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of new and relapse TB cases. This is reported quarterly and annually, using NTP records. 21. The percentage of children under 5 years who are household TB contacts and eligible for LTBI treatment is calculated as the number of such children who started LTBI treatment multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of eligible children under 5 years who are household contacts of TB cases. This is reported quarterly and annually, using facility registers. 22. The coverage of TB rapid diagnosis is calculated as the number of new and relapse TB cases diagnosed using WHO-recommended rapid tests multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of new and relapse TB cases notified. This is reported monthly, quarterly, and annually, using TB laboratory registers. 23. The coverage of drug susceptibility testing for fluoroquinolones and second-line injectable agents is calculated as the number of TB cases with rifampicin resistance and drug susceptibility testing results for fluoroquinolones and second-line injectable agents multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of TB cases with rifampicin resistance. This is reported monthly, quarterly, and annually, using TB laboratory registers. 24. The coverage of HIV testing among TB cases is calculated as the number of new and relapse TB cases with documented HIV status multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of new and relapse TB cases notified. This is reported monthly, quarterly, and annually, using facility registers. 25. The coverage of TB contact investigation is calculated as the number of contacts of TB cases who were evaluated for TB multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of contacts of TB cases identified. This is reported monthly, quarterly, and annually, using facility registers. 26. The coverage of LTBI treatment is calculated as the number of people living with HIV and children under 5 years who are household contacts of TB cases and started LTBI treatment multiplied by 100, divided by the total number of such individuals identified. This is reported monthly, quarterly, and annually, using facility registers. Data is analyzed separately for each group. 27. Digital technologies in TB care and prevention are applied based on the availability of computers, technical support, mobile broadband internet, and smartphones with video capacity. These technologies support monitoring, evaluation, distance learning for health workers, diagnostic aids, social media engagement, telemedicine, and electronic surveillance of adverse events.
